Can we transition their account log-in to MyChart? Establishing a clear framework for discovering which AI-generated notes can be accurately filed into the relevant sections of EPIC will ensure that critical clinical information from member and coach interactions is consistently captured, organized, and accessible. This will enhance care delivery by providing clinicians with timely and structured documentation, improve compliance with regulatory and organizational standards, and streamline workflows by reducing manual effort and errors. Ultimately, this approach will unlock the full potential of AI-driven documentation, supporting better patient outcomes and operational efficiency.

Description:
Participants:
Prakash, Ravi C, Adil, Jennifer, Imisa, Ananda, Sapna, Salena, Janet, Shenyan, Donald T, JunaidTechnical Lead: Raymond B.

Problem Statement:
A long-standing integration gap between Care Engine and Epic has resulted in inaccurate and incomplete delivery of Care Considerations (CCs) to clinical teams. Epic is not notified when CCs become historic or retracted, allowing outdated guidance to remain actionable. At the same time, valid CCs are missed due to flawed incremental and sequencing logic. Severity 1 CCs are further blocked by enrollment and responsible-user dependencies, conflicting with Policy 133 delivery requirements. Increased CC volume and visibility have elevated this from a technical defect to a clinical safety, operational, and compliance risk

Business Value:
Prevents clinicians from acting on outdated or invalid CCs, Ensures Severity 1 CCs are delivered within required timelines per Policy 133, regardless of enrollment, Reduces manual cleanup, duplicate CC generation, and workflow confusion and Ensures Epic reflects accurate, complete, and actionable CC information

Contacts/Dependencies:
Epic Integration TeamCareEngine EngineeringLCC Clinical OperationsIO Platform / Integration ServicesCM (Care Management) Product & OpsScope: 1. Close the Feedback LoopEpic must send CC disposition back to CareEngine that a CC was communicated/delivered in EPICDisposition codes to be reviewed to make sure all the disposition codes are mapped in ODS or notThis prevents duplicate CC generation and infinite loops 4. Prevent Delivery of Invalid CCs in EPIC by Clinical OperationsWhen a CC becomes historic or retracted, Epic must automatically cancel or remove the associated taskVisibility of historic/retracted status to end users can see it in EPICAgreed direction:Remove the task/CC in EPIC when CC becomes HIST or Retracted 5. Deliver Severity 1 CCs Regardless of EnrollmentSeverity 1 CCs must trigger task creation even if the member is not enrolled in LCCDuplicate task creation must be preventedEnrollment status must not block deliveryAgreed direction:All Sev 1 CCs must trigger task creation, regardless of LCC enrollment or responsible user.If no coach exists, task should be routed to a pool/bucket for supervisor assignment. 6. Summary: Health Advisor report - migrating Teradata table to BigQuery Phase 2
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
CSS and RetroDUR are planned for retirement in Q2 2026. Their replacement application, Clinical Rx Manager (CRxM), is scheduled to go live in mid to late Q2 2026.Once CRxM becomes the active system, it will begin sending all data to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) instead of the legacy data sources. To ensure uninterrupted downstream consumption, analytics, and reporting, the current EDW processes must transition from sourcing data in the legacy CSS/RetroDUR environments to sourcing data directly from GCP-hosted CRxM datasets.This feature ensures that data pipelines, transformations, and datasets dependent on CSS/RetroDUR structures are updated to reflect the new CRxM data model, including any changes to table names, data types, and relationships.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Implementing this feature will:Ensure continuity of EDW processing after CSS and RetroDUR retirement.Align data sourcing with the CRxM architecture and prevent data gaps.Support long-term maintainability by adopting modern GCP data structures.Mitigate business risk by proactively updating pipelines ahead of legacy decommissioning.Expected areas of change include:Table Name Changes - CRxM datasets will differ from existing EDW table structures.Data Type Changes - Source system transformations may require schema updates.Relationship Changes - Join logic may change due to revised CRxM data modeling.

Contacts/Dependencies:
CRxM Product Team - Source system owners, data model documentationGCP Data Engineering - Pipeline availability, dataset accessCSS / RetroDUR Retirement Program - Timeline for sunset activitiesEDW Architecture - Approvals and data lineage validationDownstream Consumer Teams - Validation and UAT of updated datasets

In Scope:
The following legacy EDW views and relationships must be evaluated and transitioned to GCP-sourced CRxM equivalents:DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_DLY_HIST as d DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_CPG_HIST as g on d.clnt_pgm_id = g.clnt_pgm_id -- get lvl3_acct_gid for the associated cpg_id; cpg_id is not PK; cpg_id can be mapped to multiple lvl3_acct_id DWU_EDW_RB.V_QL_CLNT_ACCT_HRCHY as h on g.CPG_ID = h.CPG_ID DWU_EDW_RB.V_CLNT_ACCT_DENORM as clnt on h.LVL3_ACCT_GID = clnt.LVL3_ACCT_GID DWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_CLNT_PGM_CMPNT_HIST as p on d.clnt_pgm_id = p.clnt_pgm_idDWU_EDW_RB.V_CSS_PGM_CMPNT_HIST as c on p.clnt_pgm_cmpnt_cd = c.pgm_cmpnt_cd

Out of Scope:

Assumptions:
These assumptions outline what must be true for this feature to succeed:CRxM will deliver complete and validated data models to EDW before integration work begins.All required CRxM datasets will be available and accessible in GCP within the expected timeline.EDW will receive accurate mapping documentation from CRxM to reconcile differences with legacy CSS/RetroDUR schemas.No additional legacy data backfill is required beyond what CRxM provides.Data governance, security roles, and GCP access will be in place prior to development.Downstream consumers will participate in UAT for validation and certification of new GCP-sourced datasets.Existing business logic remains valid unless CRxM explicitly defines a new rule or structure.

Outstanding Questions:

Success Criteria:
& Metrics:This feature is considered successful when:All CSS and RetroDUR dependencies for the listed EDW tables are fully replaced with CRxM/GCP equivalents.EDW pipelines process CRxM data successfully and without interruption.All schema changes (tables, datatypes, relationships) are updated and validated.Downstream reports and dashboards continue to function correctly with CRxM-sourced data.Data quality checks meet established thresholds with no material gaps.Historical and current data align with expected business definitions.All business stakeholders sign off that the new pipelines can replace legacy sourcing before CSS/RetroDUR retirement.The system is ready before the CRxM go-live window (mid-late Q2 2026).

Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Who: Multiple teams currently involved in the PID and OA/Recon processes, including healthcare analysts and program coordinators.What: The current processes for condition identification and reconciliation are fragmented across teams and systems. Benefit Hypothesis:
By unifying the PID and OA/Recon processes into the HIAAS platform, the organization will streamline operations, reduce the time and effort required for condition identification and reconciliation, and improve data accuracy. This will lead to better targeting of clinical programs, enhanced client satisfaction, and increased program effectiveness.

Contacts/Dependencies:
Development Team: Responsible for implementing the integration of PID and OA/Recon processes into the HIAAS platform.Data Management Team: To oversee the integration of data sources and ensure data accuracy in the ADW.Quality Assurance Team: To validate the functionality and ensure it meets user needs.Client Relations Team: To communicate findings and insights to clients effectively.

In Scope:
Overall (Epic)Integration of PID (Condition Identification based on Eligibility, Medical Claims, and Drug Claims) into the HIAAS platform.Integration of EarlierID (Condition identification based on Specialty Dispense data) into the HIAAS platform.Integration of OA (Condition identification for potential members associated with the Accordant program) into the HIAAS platform.Implementation of the reconciliation process (Recon) to analyze cost savings per member for clients.All processes designed based on the approved design solution provided as part of the feature.Automation of error flagging via control tables to catch missing members immediately. IO Scope:Rule testing and coverage for existing and new clinical rulesClinical rule testing for the accordant - 21 existing plus 9 new conditions will be covered by different rule testing featureDependenciesClinical Team: Clinical rules for the accordant program identification or conditions

Out of Scope:

Summary: Automated file count reconciliation between IMS & ODS - MAH tracker data - Impact Incentives
Description:
This is not MAH L3 Prod support. Please find another parent This feature would also address the prod defect DE366234: IMS file processing enhancement to ETL jobWe need IMS batch file transfer process to be enhanced by IMS team and tested with ETL and S&O to close the defect.

Problem Statement:
IMS sends thousands (3000 to 5000) of third party tracker data files daily to ODS, occasionally there are issues in file transfer process leads to missing tracker data files loaded in ODS impact MAH Incentives downstream, which leads to production incidents to trace back the missed files. There is no mechanism today to automatically confirm number of files sent from IMS source all are received, processed & loaded to ODS. Temporarily S&O team has a manual process via spread sheet to tracking the file count coordinating with IMS source system on a daily basis.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Outcome of this feature is to ensure MAH Incentive member experience is not negatively impacted due to internal system level file transfer failures. Develop an Automated file count reconciliation between IMS & ODS and eliminate S&O teams manual effort. Alert S&O team if there are discrepancies, so that S&O team take timely action to recover missing tracker data files working with network/Sftp team.

Contacts/Dependencies:
IMS

In Scope:
IMS Scope: IMS to send file counts to ODS system.Generate trigger / touch file & the counts as a last step of IMS file transfer. CDP Scope:Develop an alert mechanism to notify S&O team when number of files received in ODS is less than IMS source file count, so that S&O team approach network/SFTP team to re-send the files failed to transfer for given date. Network/SFTP team preserve files 60 days. Missing files needs to be reprocessed within 60 days window.

Notes:
from 1/6 meeting between CPD, IMS and S&O teamsOption 1: The IMS team will analyze the feasibility of sending tracker data files once per day (currently sent twice daily).If once-daily transmission is feasible, include the total file count either within the trigger file or in a separate count file.If the count is included in the trigger file, a separate count file will not be required.The trigger file containing the file count should be generated and transmitted as the final step, after all data files have been produced and sent. Option 2: If IMS is unable to implement a once-daily file transmission, a Batch ID can be used to correlate the data files with their corresponding trigger file containing the file count. Additional NotesThe file count will help automate the currently manual process that uses spreadsheets to track file counts.At the network/SFTP level, up to three retries are currently attempted for file transfers.In some cases, retries fail, requiring the network team to manually retransmit failed files.If a file mismatch is identified, coordination with the network/SFTP team will still be required for retransmission, as it is done currently.The network team retains files for up to 60 days. Next StepsThe IMS team will schedule a follow-up call next week to review the options and determine the approach to move forward with implementation. Rohitabh will set up next meeting.

Summary: Akamai mobile SDK integration
Description:
SummaryIntegrate the Akamai React Native SDK into the MyActiveHealth mobile app so that every outbound HTTPS API request carries an Akamai-issued secure header (bot/integrity token). These headers will be validated at the Akamai edge to provide an additional layer of protection against bot traffic, request replay, and unauthorized API access.

Business Value:
Strengthens API security posture by enabling Akamai edge-level request validation on all mobile-originated traffic.Reduces risk of automated abuse, scraping, and credential-stuffing attacks against member-facing APIs.Aligns the mobile app with the enterprise CVS security standard for trusted client attestation.DescriptionThe Akamai React Native SDK generates a cryptographically signed header that uniquely identifies a legitimate mobile client. The mobile app must:Initialize the SDK at app startup (after native bridge is ready, before the first authenticated API call).Retrieve the secure header from the SDK on demand.Inject the header into every outbound HTTPS request issued by the app's HTTP client layer.Handle SDK initialization or header retrieval failures gracefully without blocking the user, while logging/reporting via existing error pipelines (logReport, Instrumentation.reportError).In ScopeAdding the Akamai React Native SDK (provided by the CVS Security team) as a dependency in ahm-mep-ui-mobile.Native linking and configuration for both iOS (Podfile, Info.plist) and Android (build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml).Creating a wrapper utility (e.g., src/utils/AkamaiUtils.ts) that exposes a typed API for SDK initialization and header retrieval.Integrating the wrapper into the existing HTTP client / API request interceptor so the secure header is attached to all HTTPS requests.LaunchDarkly feature flag (akamai_secure_header_enabled) gating rollout.Error handling, logging (LOGTYPE.JSERROR / LOGTYPE.NATIVEERROR), and Instrumentation reporting for SDK failures.Unit tests for the wrapper utility and interceptor behavior.Updating envs/.env. with any required Akamai configuration values (read via react-native-config).Out of ScopeDevelopment, sourcing, or distribution of the Akamai React Native SDK package itself - this will be delivered by the CVS Security team.Server-side Akamai route configuration / header validation rules - owned by the Akamai / Platform team.Changes to the ahm-mep-ui-shared-core package (this is a native-dependent integration and must live in ahm-mep-ui-mobile only).Backend API contract changes.

Business Value:
This feature ensures that the most recent tracker data (last 7 days) is prioritized and made available to MAH in near real-time. It also introduces additional optimizations for handling incoming tracker data to prevent system bottlenecks and improve overall data processing efficiency.

Background:
/ History: As part of feature F227584, the CDP Data Platform previously implemented (Feb release) a process to handle the last 180 days of Validic device data and load it into the tracker database.This enhancement was required due to a production issue in mid-January when Validic unexpectedly sent a large volume of device data after users upgraded to the latest iOS version. In many cases, devices synchronized historical data going back as far as 2016, triggering a large influx of messages: Wearable Device -> Validic -> Real-time ingest (ODS/GCP) -> API -> MMAH. This backlog created message congestion and impacted production performance.

Problem Statement:

The existing experience allows users to bypass meaningful engagement by completing HRAs without reviewing or updating responses. Additionally, reset capabilities in the legacy/on-prem system are inconsistent, overly reliant on backend configurations, and not standardized across programs. A modernized, scalable approach is required to ensure regular HRA completion, improve data accuracy, and drive meaningful member engagement. HRA reset is also needed to continue to incentivize members by requiring them to retake the HRA.DependenciesBackend implementation for reset logic (CDP, COP)Alignment with Custom HRA feature for future integrationIncentives to make the Reset HRA activity available in the Health Checklist.This is current functionality that shows up based on the planned program yearEmail communications for members to Retake the HRA in the New Plan Year (IO)UI/UX updates for member engagement and retake flow?Phase 1: Guided HRA Retake with Pre-Populated Responses

Introduce a standardized HRA reset experience that requires members to intentionally review their HRA responses without forcing them to start from scratch.Approach:In Phase 1, the HRA will be reset for the new program year, but the member's previously submitted answers will be pre-populated. Members will be required to navigate through every question, review their prior responses, make updates where needed, and complete the HRA. This avoids creating unnecessary burden for members while still ensuring they actively validate and refresh their health information. Because asking all members to retake a 40+ question HRA with blank responses may negatively impact completion. A pre-populated review experience provides a balanced approach - it supports data validation while maintaining a reasonable user experience.Member Experience:Member sees a clear activity such as “Retake your HRA”Prior HRA answers are displayed/pre-populatedMember must go through each question in the HRAMember can keep or update existing answersMember must complete the full review flow before the HRA is considered completedActivity may be surfaced as a Tile in Todays activities in Pathways Health Checklist, Pathways, Profile, and supported through email communicationsUpon completion the Tiles goes awayThe MyHealth100 tile will still be visible for users in the Pathways home page with ""Take health assessment"" or ""Retake health assessment"".

Business Value:
<Business Value descriptor here>We don't know how members are getting to login - whether they tapped an email link, a push notification, or just opened the app directly. That means we can't tell if our re-engagement campaigns are actually driving authentication, and we can't segment login funnel performance by channel. The data just doesn't exist today. Since the emails and PNs are deep linking members directly into MyActiveHealth (MAH), we currently do not have a way to identify or track members who enter MAH by clicking those email deep links. Once the member lands in MAH-especially after authentication or SSO-the entry source is lost.This creates multiple gaps:We cannot measure the effectiveness of emails in driving MAH traffic and engagementWe cannot differentiate email-driven engagement from organic or direct trafficProduct, marketing, and business teams lack data to optimize email CTAs, timing, content, and destination experiencesIssues tied specifically to email entry (drop-offs, navigation errors, authentication friction) are harder to detect and diagnoseAs a result, we are improving the front-door experience without visibility into how members are entering MAH or whether these email initiatives are delivering measurable impact.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If we capture and store login source at the point of authentication, we can start answering questions we currently can't: which channel drives higher login success rates, where mid-flow drop-offs are happening by source, and whether email vs. push is actually moving members. Longer term, this is the foundation for smarter re-engagement targeting and more honest campaign reporting. If MAH captures and persists email deep-link attribution through the full entry and authentication flow, then Product, Marketing, and Business teams will be able to accurately measure email-driven traffic and engagement, identify and resolve email-specific experience issues faster, and use data to optimize email strategies-resulting in improved member engagement and clearer visibility into impact.

Summary: Profile Redesign
Description:
Problem Statement:
MAH's current Profile experience contains a mix of standard profile management functions and wellness engagement experiences such as Coaching and Mental Health Check-In. As additional health and wellness capabilities are introduced and consolidated within the new MyPath experience, Profile is no longer the appropriate destination for these journey-based features.Members primarily expect Profile to serve as a destination for managing personal information, account settings, communication preferences, health records, connected devices, and support-related functions. Housing coaching and mental well-being experiences within Profile creates inconsistency in navigation, reduces discoverability of wellness resources, and blurs the distinction between account management and health journey management.To create a more intuitive information architecture, MAH will simplify the Profile experience by focusing it on core profile and account management capabilities while relocating Coaching and Mental Health Check-In experiences to the new MyPath destination. Summary: OTP Error Messaging & Login CTA Feedback States
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Show members how many OTP attempts remain on failure, and add loading/confirmation states to all primary login CTAs to eliminate perceived unresponsiveness.

Problem Statement:
Failed OTP submissions return a vague error with no attempt count - members don't know whether to retry or request a new code. Primary login CTAs (Send Code, Continue, Login) have no loading or disabled state, so multiple taps trigger duplicate API calls and the app feels frozen. Both gaps are cited directly in app store reviews.

Benefit Hypothesis:
These are front-end-only fixes on the same screens, deliverable in one sprint by the same team. Fixing the error message reduces OTP drop-off; fixing CTA states eliminates duplicate calls and unresponsiveness complaints - two of the top-ranked login pain points from review analysis. figma: https://www.figma.com/design/1Pk0rgJGqXB4VWkEDdCb9N/My-Active-Health-UX?node-id=40053635-32646&t=grvun59Lv4RpHKxQ-0

In Scope:
On OTP failure, display inline error: 'Invalid code. You have [X] of [N] attempts left before a new code is required.' Values must be dynamically populated from the backend response. If the backend returns an out-of-range attempt count, fall back to: 'Invalid code. Please try again or request a new code.' - copy to be approved by UX. On new OTP generation (user-requested or session expiry), reset the attempt counter and clear the previous error immediately without a page reload. Error messaging applies to Email OTP and Phone OTP flows only - identical wording, placement, and behavior across Web, iOS, and Android. All primary login CTAs (Send Code, Resend Code, Continue, Login) must enter a visually distinct loading state immediately on tap - spinner, label change, or opacity shift (Design to specify). CTAs must be non-interactive while a request is in-flight - no second API call may be dispatched regardless of how many times the user taps. On successful Send/Resend Code, show a confirmation state (checkmark or 'Code Sent' label) for a minimum of 1.5 seconds before advancing or resetting. On backend error, return the CTA to its default interactive state and display the inline error - button must never be left permanently disabled.

Out of Scope:
<Bulleted out-of-scope items here>OTP lockout duration, lockout logic, or attempt limit configuration - backend policy, not in scope. Aetna SSO, Passcode, and third-party auth method error states. Backend API changes - this feature consumes the existing attempt count field in the response payload.

Success Criteria:
& Metrics: <Definition of Done here>OTP-step drop-off decreases Duplicate Send Code API calls decreases Support tickets tagged 'invalid code' or 'unresponsive login button' decrease

Summary: Reposition 'Remember Me' Checkbox to Pre-Login Step
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Move 'Remember Me' to the first login screen so members can set their session preference before authenticating, increasing feature utilisation.

Problem Statement:
The checkbox sits at the final login step - after credentials and OTP are entered - where most members have already stopped reading. It is chronically underutilised as a result. Members who miss it must log out and back in to retroactively set it.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Moving the checkbox to where members are making setup decisions (first screen, email entry) will surface it at the right moment. Higher utilisation reduces repeat full-login events, which is a known friction driver for engagement drop-off. No backend changes required.

In Scope:
Reposition the 'Remember Me' checkbox to the username/email entry screen, below the input field and above the primary CTA, visible within the default viewport without scrolling. Default state must remain unchecked - no pre-selection based on prior behavior, device type, or any other signal. Checkbox state must persist as a form variable through all subsequent login steps (OTP, biometric) - navigating forward or back must not reset it. On successful authentication, the checkbox value must be passed correctly to the session management layer - no change to session duration or token logic. Design must provide updated first-step login screen specs for all three platforms.

Out of Scope:
<Bulleted out-of-scope items here>Session duration, token expiry, refresh logic, or any backend session configuration. 'Remember Me' behavior within the Aetna SSO login path. Auto-populating or pre-checking the box based on device trust or session history. Redesign of the first-step login screen beyond repositioning the checkbox.

Success Criteria:
& Metrics: <Definition of Done here>'Remember Me' utilisation rate increasesNo regression in session behaviorCheckbox visible without scroll on all supported screen sizes across Web, iOS, and Android

Assumptions:
<Bulleted assumption items here>Checkbox value can be held in client-side form state from step 1 through final auth submission - no intermediate API call needed. Moving the element requires no changes to the auth API contract or backend session handling. Design specs will be available before Sprint 1 planning and won't require changes to shared layout components.

Use Cases:
Member opens login -> sees 'Remember Me' unchecked on email entry screen -> checks it -> completes OTP -> is remembered on next visit. Member checks 'Remember Me' -> navigates back to step 1 -> checkbox remains checked -> re-advances -> correct value submitted on auth. Member on shared device -> leaves checkbox unchecked -> session expires per standard timeout -> not remembered.

Summary: Passkey UX Improvements — Navigation, Opt-Out & iOS Auto-Launch
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Fix three compounding Passkey UX gaps: a navigation dead-end, a missing persistent opt-out, and a broken iOS auto-launch.

Problem Statement:
Members who tap 'Login with Other Options' from the Passkey screen have no way back - they must restart the entire login flow. Members who dismiss the Passkey setup prompt see it again on every login with no way to decline permanently. On iOS, registered Passkey members must manually tap to invoke biometrics - Android auto-launches; iOS does not. All three are flagged in app store reviews.

Benefit Hypothesis:
All three gaps share a root cause: the Passkey flow was shipped without handling non-happy-path member behavior. Consolidating them into one feature lets a single iOS/auth engineering team fix the Passkey component once, run one regression suite, and ship a materially improved experience in a single release.

In Scope:
NAVIGATION - Render a Back control on the 'Login with Other Options' screen: iOS back chevron in nav bar; Android on-screen button + system back gesture. NAVIGATION - Back must return the member to the initial login selection screen (Passkey vs. Other Options) - not restart the flow or clear any pre-populated fields. NAVIGATION - Re-entering 'Other Options' after navigating back must present a clean state - no cached errors or stale input. OPT-OUT - Add an unchecked 'Do not ask me again' control to the Passkey setup prompt - must be visible without scrolling, never pre-selected. OPT-OUT - Activating opt-out suppresses the Passkey setup prompt on that device for 90 calendar days - persists across app restarts, OS updates, and app version updates. OPT-OUT - Opt-out is stored per member-device - opting out on Device A must not suppress the prompt on Device B. OPT-OUT - Members who opt out must be able to set up Passkey at any time via Settings without logging out. OPT-OUT - After 90 days, the prompt resumes at login only - never mid-session. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - On app open, if a valid Passkey is registered on that device, automatically invoke the system biometric prompt via ASAuthorizationController after the splash screen, before the login screen idles. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - If the member dismisses the auto-invoked prompt, fall back to the standard login screen - do not re-invoke in the same session. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - If no Passkey is registered, or the app is opened via deep link or push notification, suppress auto-launch and show the standard login screen. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - Validate on iOS 16, 17, and 18 across all supported iPhone and iPad form factors.

Out of Scope:
<Bulleted out-of-scope items here>Passkey registration and enrollment flow - post-enrollment experience only. Android auto-launch - already working correctly. Face ID / Touch ID permission prompts - managed by iOS OS layer. Admin or plan-level overrides of member opt-out preference.

Success Criteria:
& Metrics: <Definition of Done here>Passkey funnel completion rate increases Passkey prompt dismissal-without-opt-out events decrease iOS Passkey login completion rate increases attributed to auto-launch. 0 post-launch defects: no navigation loops, opt-out not persisting, or auto-launch misfiring on deep-link opens.

Assumptions:
<Bulleted assumption items here>Login flow is a nav stack - adding a Back pop action does not require flow re-architecture. Member identifier / session state is preserved on the stack and survives back-forward navigation without a new auth handshake. Opt-out preference can be stored in UserDefaults (iOS) / SharedPreferences (Android) and will survive app updates for 90 days. Reinstall behavior must be documented before launch. Passkey registration status is readable from the device Keychain without a network call, enabling auto-launch before network-dependent UI loads. Legal and Security approve suppressing the Passkey prompt for 90 days - must be confirmed before Sprint 1. Apple App Store Review Guidelines permit auto-invoking biometrics on app open for enrolled members - engineering to confirm before development begins.

Use Cases:
NAVIGATION - Member taps 'Login with Other Options' -> taps Back -> returned to Passkey vs. Other Options screen -> selects Passkey -> completes biometric auth. NAVIGATION - Android member uses system back gesture from Other Options -> identical result to tapping Back. OPT-OUT - Member dismisses Passkey prompt with 'Do not ask me again' checked -> prompt absent for next 90 days on that device -> resumes after expiry. OPT-OUT - Member opts out on iPhone -> logs in on iPad -> Passkey setup prompt appears on iPad as expected. OPT-OUT - Member changes mind -> navigates to Settings -> initiates Passkey setup without logging out. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member with registered Passkey opens app -> Face ID invoked automatically after splash -> authenticates -> lands on home screen. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member opens app via push notification -> auto-launch suppressed -> standard login screen shown -> member routes to intended destination post-auth. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member dismisses Face ID prompt -> standard login screen shown -> Face ID not re-invoked in same session.

Summary: Redesign Rewards Experience- Integrate Badges & Tiers in the rewards experience
Description:
LoB: <Requesting LoB>Platform: <Web, iOS, Android>

Business Value:
<Business Value descriptor here>By consolidating badges and tiers into Rewards experience (and by removing them from the achievements tab under Profile) we will increase user engagement with loyalty program and drive higher repeat activity. Users currently have to navigate to 2 disconnected surfaces to understand their progress and redeemable value which dilutes the motivational loop of earn -> rewards co-locating badges & tiers with tangible value should Increase rewards tab DAULift tier progression rateImprove rewards experienceReduce any related support tickets about badges & tiers

Non-Functional Requirements:
Today, badges and tier status live under the Achievements tab within the Profile section, while points, coupons, and redeemable rewards live under the Rewards experience. This creates several user and business problems: Fragmented discovery: Users earning badges are not reminded of the rewards those badges unlock, and users browsing rewards don't see how close they are to the next tier. Low visibility of the Achievements tab: Analytics show the Achievements tab under Profile receives less than 5% of Rewards tab traffic, meaning the motivational value of badges is largely invisible. Weak progression loop: Users don't associate tier benefits (bonus points, exclusive offers) with the effort of earning them because the two experiences are disconnected. Redundant navigation: Maintaining badge and tier UI in two mental locations increases cognitive load for users and design/engineering overhead for the team. The opportunity is to unify the earning narrative (badges, tiers) with the value narrative (rewards, points, redemptions) in a single, purposeful destination.

In Scope:
Rewards Experience - Additions Dedicated Badges section within Rewards, showing earned badges, locked badges with unlock criteria, and recently-earned state Tier benefits panel showing what each tier unlocks (bonus multipliers, exclusive rewards, early access) Deep links from badge earn notifications directly into the Rewards tabEmpty states for new users explaining the badges, tiers, and rewards loop Profile Experience - Removals Remove the Achievements tab from the Profile section Archive but preserve historical badge data; no data loss during migration

Out of Scope:
New badge types, new tier definitions, advanced gamification animations beyond existing patterns, and social sharing of badgesLanding Page integration with Badges and TiersSuccess Criteria & Metrics: Engagement: Rewards tab DAU increasesProgression: Lift in users advancing at least one tier quarter-over-quarter Redemption: Increase in reward redemption rate among users who view the new Status module Discoverability: More of active users view the Badges section at least once within 30 days of launch Support: Reduction in tickets tagged “badges location” or “tier status” No regression: Profile tab engagement does not drop, indicating users are finding the new location rather than getting lost Qualitative: Positive sentiment in user research sessions on the unified experience

Assumptions:
Users currently engaging with the Achievements tab will follow the migration rather than churn from the feature The existing badge and tier data models can be surfaced in the Rewards tab without backend schema changes Users associate “Rewards” as the correct mental home for status and recognition (validated via prior research; to be re-confirmed in usability testing) Notification infrastructure can be updated to deep-link to the new location without a separate release cycle

Dependencies:
Design: Final visual specs for the Status module, Badges grid, and tier benefits panel Backend: API endpoint consolidation so the Rewards tab can fetch badges, tier, and points in a single call (performance target under 400ms) Platform teams: iOS, Android, and Web engineering capacity aligned for a coordinated launch Analytics: Instrumentation framework and dashboards ready before launch for measurement

Summary: Celebration Screen Refresh for Rewards Screens (Lightweight, Auto‑Dismiss)
Description:
Problem Statement:
Today, every reward-earning or milestone event in MyActiveHealth interrupts the member with a full-page Celebration screen. This pattern is used across multiple distinct scenarios spanning generic reward earns (hearts / gems), Pathway progression, delayed Health Checklist rewards, Explore feedback, Challenges, Mental Health check-ins, and Coaching. The full-page takeover forces a dismissal step, breaks task flow, repeats confetti/animation fatigue, and - most critically - is inappropriate for negative mood check-ins where the current celebratory treatment is emotionally tone-deaf.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Reduce friction: members complete their in-progress task without a blocking modal, improving completion rates and perceived app responsiveness. Consistent reinforcement: a single lightweight snack bar + confetti pattern unifies reward feedback across Pathway, Explore, Challenges, HC, and generic triggers. Emotionally appropriate UX: negative mood / mental-health scenarios get a calm, resource-forward treatment instead of celebratory confetti. Delayed-reward clarity: HC claims-based and document-upload flows can set accurate 1-2 week and 5-6 week expectations inline, reducing member confusion and downstream support tickets. Engineering efficiency: one reusable snack-bar component replaces 16 screen variants, lowering long-term maintenance and enabling faster rollout via a single LaunchDarkly flag.

In Scope:
Replace the full-page Celebration screen with a non-blocking snack-bar component for all distinct scenarios listed in the Scope table. Confetti animation appears with the snack bar for positive celebratory scenarios and respects prefers-reduced-motion. Reward-type awareness: snack bar renders hearts, gems, or no reward icon depending on the trigger payload. Delayed-reward messaging for HC scenarios , communicating the 1-2 week or 5-6 week wait window. Mental-health branch: positive mood check -> content recommendation CTA in the snack bar; negative mood check -> emergency-resources CTA with no confetti and neutral styling. Drum-roll pre-reveal animation (scenario 15) plays inline before the snack bar appears, not as a full-page takeover. LaunchDarkly flag controls the entire refresh, allowing per-environment (QA / UAT / Production) and gradual rollout. Amplitude instrumentation for snack-bar impressions, CTA taps, auto-dismiss, and manual dismiss across all scenarios.

Accessibility:
ARIA live region announcement, keyboard dismissal, screen-reader parity (VoiceOver / TalkBack), WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, and minimum 44×44 touch targets. Suppression of legacy celebration modal, Badge/Tier full-page overlays previously tied to the old Celebration flow, and any duplicate confetti when the snack bar is active.

Out of Scope:
Redesign of the reward system itself (hearts, gems, tier logic, claim eligibility rules). Back-end changes to HC claims or document-upload reward calculation windows. New celebration triggers beyond the listed scenarios. Changes to the Badge / Tier earning logic - only the visual celebration treatment is suppressed. Email, push, or SMS celebration notifications. Localization of new copy beyond existing supported locales (English only at launch).

Use Cases:
A member completes a Pathway goal check-in and sees a snack bar confirming +hearts without leaving the Pathway screen . A member finishes a Pathway level or the full Pathway and receives unified snack-bar acknowledgment . A member completes an HC claims-based activity and is told via snack bar that their reward will arrive in 5-6 weeks. A member uploads an HC document and is told via snack bar that their reward will arrive in 1-2 weeks. A member rates an Explore item (Video / Audio / Article / Recipe / Wellness Webinar) and sees a snack bar confirming hearts or gems earned. A member hits a Challenge milestone and is celebrated inline without leaving the challenge view . A member submits a positive mood check-in and is offered relevant content recommendations in the snack bar. A member submits a negative mood check-in and is gently pointed to emergency resources in a non-celebratory snack bar. A member earning a reward sees a brief drum-roll animation before the snack bar reveals the outcome . A QA / product engineer toggles the LaunchDarkly flag in QA, UAT, or Production and verifies the new treatment without code redeploy. A screen-reader user hears the snack-bar content announced via an ARIA live region and can dismiss it via keyboard.

Assumptions:
The existing snack-bar component from F233336 (Explore Celebration Refresh) is reusable and will be extended, not rebuilt, for the remaining scenarios. A single LaunchDarkly flag will gate the refresh; scenario-level sub-flags are not required for launch but will be discussed with UX. The reward payload (type, amount, delayed-reward window) is provided by existing back-end services without API changes. Confetti assets and animation timings follow the reduced-motion guidelines established for F233336. Mental-health emergency-resource content is sourced from the existing resource catalog maintained by the Clinical team. Scenario 16 (Coaching) UX copy and reward mapping will be confirmed by the Coaching product stream before development completion. Amplitude event taxonomy will extend existing celebration events with a 'surface: snack_bar' property rather than introducing a new event family. acceptance aligns with WCAG 2.1 AA; VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) are the reference screen readers. LoB: <Requesting LoB>Platform: <Web, iOS, Android>

Problem Statement:
MAH currently relies on Mobile Network Operator (MNO)-based identity proofing and one-time passcode (OTP) challenges to perform step-up authentication for sensitive post-login actions. This approach is limited to members who have a phone number on file and does not provide a high-assurance identity verification signal. Additionally, OTP-based verification remains dependent on phone ownership and may be vulnerable to risks such as SIM-swap attacks or message interception.As a result, there is a coverage gap for members who cannot be verified through MNO-based methods or who require stronger identity assurance before performing sensitive actions. Currently, MAH does not provide a mechanism to verify identity using a government-issued credential.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If myActiveHealth introduces Mobile Driver's License (mDL) verification as an alternative step-up authentication method, then members can verify their identity using a higher-assurance government-issued credential stored in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. This will expand verification coverage beyond phone-dependent methods, improve confidence in sensitive transactions, and allow the organization to evaluate member adoption and usability before considering broader deployment or future OTP replacement.

Summary: Enabler - Rewards Resolution Assistant
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Rewards-related inquiries represent the largest category of member support requests within MyActiveHealth. Recent incident ticket analysis shows that many rewards issues are not true system defects, but repeatable questions caused by limited visibility, unclear program rules, processing timelines, eligibility requirements, and redemption expectations.Members frequently contact support to understand why points are missing or delayed, whether an activity has been completed, what rewards they are eligible for, how to redeem rewards, or when they can expect to receive a payout. Because rewards programs can vary by client, program type, incentive model, activity rules, and payout method, members currently lack a centralized, self-service capability that can provide accurate answers based on their specific rewards configuration.As a result, routine and explainable questions often become support tickets, creating unnecessary operational overhead, increasing resolution time, and reducing member confidence in the rewards experience.MyActiveHealth needs a program-aware Rewards Resolution Assistant that can guide members through a predefined set of high-frequency rewards questions and provide the latest applicable answers based on their program type, reward status, and activity completion information.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If MyActiveHealth introduces a guided, program-aware Rewards Resolution Assistant that provides accurate answers to the most common rewards questions, then members will be able to self-serve routine rewards inquiries without contacting support.This will improve member transparency and trust in the rewards experience, reduce avoidable Rewards/Incentive support tickets, decrease operational overhead for support teams, and allow product and engineering teams to focus on true defects and higher-value enhancements.Success will be measured by:Reduction in Rewards/Incentive support ticket volumeIncrease in self-service completion rate for rewards inquiriesDecrease in repeat or duplicate rewards-related contactsImproved member satisfaction with rewards clarity and guidanceReduction in support escalations for routine program rule or status questions

Contacts/Dependencies:

In Scope:
Create a Phase 1 Rewards Resolution Assistant within MyActiveHealth focused on guided self-service support for rewards-related questions.Provide members with a predefined set of high-frequency rewards questions based on recent incident ticket patterns.Tailor answers based on the member's rewards program type and configuration.Support program-aware responses for key rewards variables, including:Dollar or Points or hearts-based programsGift card-based programsHRA/HSA payout programsPaycheck or employer-funded payout programsPrograms with no incentive configuredReporting ONLY INCV program.Provide guided answers for common rewards questions, including:Missing or delayed points/hearts/DollarPending activity creditCompleted vs. remaining reward activitiesReward eligibilityReward redemption processGift card or payout timingMaximum reward limitsProgram year and deadline guidanceDisplay member-specific reward information where available, including:Current reward balanceCompleted activitiesPending activitiesRemaining eligible activitiesReward type or payout methodProgram year informationUse controlled, predefined response templates to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance.Provide clear next steps when the assistant cannot resolve the inquiry through self-service.Escalate members to the appropriate support path when the question requires manual review or data correction.

Out of Scope:
Open-ended, free-form AI chatbot experience in Phase 1.AI-generated responses without predefined and approved templates.Automatic reward adjustments, manual overrides, or points corrections.Backend changes to reward calculation, reward eligibility, or payout processing logic.Replacing existing support teams or support workflows.Resolving complex edge cases that require manual investigation.Processing uploads or proof-of-completion documents in Phase 1.Real-time vendor issue remediation or vendor-side ticket creation.Proactive notifications or alerts for missing points, restored points, or pending activities.Full natural language intent detection across all possible rewards questions.Support for non-rewards-related MyActiveHealth issues, such as login, device sync, coaching, or general account support, unless directly tied to rewards guidance.

Without clearly defined and enforced Security and Non-Functional Requirements, the platform risks inconsistent client experiences, security vulnerabilities, regulatory exposure, and reduced trust from enterprise clients.

Benefit Hypothesis:
By having industry-standard Security and NFR's for the Client Self-Service Portal, we will enable employer representatives to safely and confidently customize the client experience on the MAH platform. As a result, the platform will deliver a consistent, secure, and scalable experience that reduces security and compliance risk, improves client trust, supports enterprise adoption, and allows the portal to scale efficiently without increasing operational or support burden.

Summary: AHM BoB End-to-End testing - data sourced from Unified Onboarding Platform
Description:
Participants:
Prakash, Ravi, Ananda, Ray, John Israel, Adil, Junaid, Shenyan, Jordan, Andrew Z, Sai, Chintan, Jennifer, Priya, Jay, Rohith, Sridevi, Divyank, Veda & Jude, Ajith, Naziba, Sachin, Sundar, Anu, Arun, Rajesh, Mrudula, Maha, Alen, Eric, Mothi, Kishore, Arun, Mohd, Ganesh, Nithya, SendilRTE/PM: MeetaBusiness Lead: Jennifer Daniels, Lynette This feature tracks and enables participation of all ActiveHealth Management (AHM) products and their associated applications in Book of Business (BoB) end-to-end (E2E) testing, using data sourced from the Unified Onboarding Platform. The Unified Onboarding Platform serves as the single source of truth for onboarding data and configurations required to support client implementations across AHM product lines, including but not limited to AHM, TDC, and Weight Management. The specific scope of this feature is to ensure that AHM products are fully onboarded to Unified Onboarding Platform and can reliably consume onboarding data to support comprehensive E2E testing of Book of Business scenarios. This includes validating data readiness, integration points, and downstream application participation required for successful testing execution. E2E timeline: Entire month of August (8/3 to 8/31)

Benefit Hypothesis:
Improved Test Coverage & Participation VisibilityIf all AHM products and associated applications are onboarded through the Unified Onboarding Platform for Book of Business (BoB) E2E testing,then we will achieve complete visibility into participation status,resulting in improved test coverage and reduced risk of missed integrations. Early Detection of Integration GapsIf participation tracking is enforced before and during E2E testing,then missing integrations or incomplete onboarding will be identified early,resulting in fewer defects in downstream environments and production. Reduction in Data Inconsistencies Across SystemsIf BoB E2E testing data is sourced from a single unified onboarding platform,then inconsistencies caused by fragmented data sources will decrease,resulting in higher data accuracy across downstream applications (MAH, Care Engine, Epic, etc.). Faster Onboarding and Test Execution CyclesIf participation tracking is centralized and standardized,then product and application onboarding into BoB testing will be faster and more streamlined,resulting in reduced cycle time for end-to-end validation. Enhanced Accountability and TraceabilityIf participation status of each AHM product/application is explicitly tracked,then ownership gaps and unclear responsibilities will be minimized,resulting in improved accountability across Product, Engineering, and QA teams. Improved Reporting for Leadership & GovernanceIf participation metrics are captured centrally,then leadership will have real-time visibility into testing readiness and gaps,resulting in better decision-making and governance over BoB readiness. Summary: Termed Supplier and Member Handling with Tracker Sync Prevention
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Two issues with termed supplier/member re: tracker sync prevention (impact: may cause delay/slowness) Issue 1: Termination status for suppliers and members is not consistently received, which prevents us from reliably stopping tracker data synchronization. Next steps for Issue 1:Need to identify current process for termination and when/where gap occurs Issue 2: Even when termination status is received, tracker data continues to sync in certain scenarios (e.g., DE373293: tracker data continues to sync despite the member being termed). Impact: These gaps create a legal and compliance risk, as data may continue to sync for suppliers or members who should no longer be processed. Short term fix for issue 2:S&O: Pick the termed members and disconnect their tracker device from backendBy 2/20, this will be completedLong term fix for issue 2:Analysis requested by business to understand impact Prevent any Tracker data from syncing to MAH for termed members/supplier while preserving auditability and minimizing operational overhead. Option 1 - CDPApproach: Use CDP (which already processes Validic data) to filter out events for termed members/suppliers and prevent forwarding data to MAHPros:Leverages existing CDP pipelines and member-status enrichmentNo application or backend changes requiredNear real-time behavior once member status is updated in CDPCons:Data from tracker devices is still sent from ValidicAlthough data is not visible in the MAH app for termed members, ingestion continues at the source level. Estimate - 30 pointsOption 2 - Digital batch disconnect (Digital and CDP)Approach: Implement a daily batch job to identify connected, termed members/suppliers and trigger a backend disconnect to stop future data ingestion from ValidicProsFully stops future data ingestion at the sourceCleaner long-term solution for data governanceCon:Additional complexity: new pub/sub implementation, backend logic, and monitoring required.EstimateCDP - 40 pointsDigital - 30 points Termed Historical DataThe S&O team will need to execute a one-time cleanup job

Summary: Trackers - Daily Maximum Limit for Connected Device
Description:
Participants:
Tech Lead:

Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
At present, there is a daily maximum limit for members who manually input their tracker measurements; however, this limit does not extend to members who are directly connected to the Modern My Active Health application through their devices. Consequently, this allows some participants to manipulate their challenge entries, giving them an unfair advantage in the rankings while others are competing fairly.

By implementing a daily maximum limit for connected device trackers within the Modern My Active Health application will lead to improved data integrity and user engagement. By capping the amount of data that can be synced each day, we expect to reduce the likelihood of data errors and processing delays, resulting in a more reliable and efficient application experience.

Summary: Pathway Enhancement: Extended Pathway Completion
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Today, once members complete all recommended learning pathways, their pathway effectively ends. This creates a dead-end experience that:Reduces engagement and retention post-completion.Prevents members from deepening or refreshing skills (e.g., content changes, knowledge decay).Blocks motivated learners from exploring adjacent or advanced pathways.Limits our ability to maintain a continuous value cycle and habit loop within the product.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If we offer members clear options to continue after completing all recommended pathways-including:Select a new pathway (recommended, trending, adjacent skills, or role-based), and/orRetake a previously completed pathway (full retake or maintenance mode focused on refreshers and updates),then we will:Increase post-completion engagement (measured by 7/30/60-day return rates and session depth).Improve learning outcomes (knowledge retention, skills validation).Boost content utilization (more pathways started/resumed).Increase satisfaction and perceived value

IO, DP, CDP

Out of Scope:
Adaptive learning beyond maintenance heuristics.Gamified leaderboards or new badging systems.

Summary: Agent-assisted gift card redemption - Update Member's Address and Contact info

Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Engagement Specialists (ES) lack the tools to efficiently support members during gift card redemptions. For a population that is not digitally savvy and might not have digital devices, email address and phone numbers ES might want to help them update their information on the call. To enhance the holistic experience for our members and improve the efficiency of Engagement Specialists (ES), we aim to implement a system that allows ES to update multiple or alternate addresses and email addresses without OTP verification. Additionally, providing easy access to previous conversation notes will enable ES to deliver accurate information and maintain continuity in support. These improvements will optimize call time and elevate overall member satisfaction.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Allowing members to update their addresses, email id and phone number will enhance their experience, particularly for those who frequently relocate, ultimately increasing member satisfaction and retention. Additionally, by implementing a dedicated ticket search capability, we hypothesize that ES will be able to access ticket information more efficiently, leading to quicker resolutions and improved communication with members.

Description:

Background:
The Intelligent Monitoring Tool (IMT) is a multi-product platform used by the Business Operations monitoring team to track 12 product lines through real-time Day-over-Day monitoring of member lives in a program and ensure business flow completed end to end for every client. It runs backend queries, populates unified user interface, and triggers configurable threshold-based alerts at three severity levels - so monitors see issues the moment they cross business thresholds. The goal is to reduce monitoring time by 30% while onboarding seven additional products onto the monitoring team - without adding headcount.

Business Value:
Onboard MAH, LCC, and MedQuery to the Intelligent Monitoring Tool (IMT) to deliver a single, real-time, business-KPI view of program health across the member journey - ingestion -> member match -> engagement -> egress -> outcomes - enabling proactive issue detection where traditional observability or application monitoring stops at system health.Operational efficiency: Reduce manual monitoring effort (currently 2.5-3 hrs/analyst); enable 1 analyst to cover all 3 programs in the same window.Proactive detection: Day-over-Day, Week-over-Week, Month-over-Month threshold alerting replaces reactive triage with early warning on ingestion gaps, member-match shortfalls, engagement dips, and outcome trend shifts.Welcome Season readiness: Validates client/member flow, eligibility, entitlement, and program activation end-to-end before campaigns go live.Business KPI lens: ""Observability detects system failures. IMT detects business failures - even when systems look healthy.""

In Scope:
Onboarding the KPI topics from the MAH / MQ / LCC Monitoring Plan to IMT.
